Hi Alice —

Thanks again for the intro. We'd love to get a 60–75 minute demo scheduled that covers (1) product walkthrough for your engineers, (2) a brief security/compliance review for your security lead, and (3) a short procurement / commercial Q&A. Because your team spans US / EU / APAC, I pulled a few options that try to maximize overlap. All times listed with PDT / CET / JST for reference.

Proposed slots (pick one or we can split into two shorter sessions):
- Option A (single session, US/EU-friendly): Thu Mar 26, 09:00 PDT / 18:00 CET / Fri Mar 27 02:00 JST
- Option B (single session, EU/APAC-friendly): Mon Mar 30, 19:00 PDT / Tue Mar 31 04:00 CET / 12:00 JST
- Option C (two shorter sessions - rotates):
  • Eng-focused (US/EU): Thu Mar 26, 08:30 PDT / 17:30 CET / 01:30 JST
  • Security/Procurement (EU-friendly): Mon Mar 30, 09:30 CET / 17:30 JST / 00:30 PDT

We can also record the engineer-focused session and do an async Q&A doc for folks who can’t attend. Attached: draft agenda and our latest SOC2 questionnaire for Bob to skim.

Attendees from our side: Mateo Alvarez (AE support / calendar), Sean Gallagher (Solutions Engineer), me (AE).

Can you confirm who will join from your side (names/roles) and which slot you prefer? If none of the above work, share a couple of constrained windows and we’ll adapt.

Thanks!

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Marissa —

Thanks for the quick options. High level on our side:
- Eng: Myself (Eng Manager, EU) + two senior SWEs based in Dublin and Amsterdam — mornings CET work best for them (09:00–12:00 CET).
- Security: Bob Singh (Security Lead, US East) — Bob is flexible but prefers mornings US time (PDT mid-day is OK for him occasionally).
- Procurement: Carol Tan (APAC procurement lead, based in Singapore) — local hours 09:00–17:00 SGT / JST; late EU afternoons are possible for her.

Given that spread, a single session will be tough for everyone. My preference is two focused sessions:
1) Eng deep-dive for engineers (include breakout for architecture questions) — aim for a US/EU overlap so our Dublin/Amsterdam engineers can join live.
2) Security + Procurement — smaller meeting where Bob and Carol can be present.

Proposed dates from our end:
- Eng session: Thu Mar 26, 09:00 PDT / 18:00 CET / Fri Mar 27 02:00 JST — that works for our EU engineers if we keep it to ~60 minutes.
- Security/Procurement: Mon Mar 30, 10:00 CET / 18:00 JST / 01:00 PDT — this is early for the US but Bob can make the first hour if needed; Carol is available late morning JST.

If those two work, can you send invites and confirm agendas for each? Also, Bob would like a high-level SOC2 summary ahead of the security session (we saw the questionnaire you attached — appreciate that).

Cheers,
Alice

Hi Alice / team —

Thanks — happy to run the engineer session. A couple of operational notes from the SE side:
- For the Eng deep-dive: 60–75 minutes works. I recommend we do a 35–40 minute product walkthrough with a live architecture Q&A/breakout for your engineers (~20 minutes). We can then keep a 10–15 minute wrap for procurement/commercial questions or hand that to Marissa/Jordan.
- Recording + shared doc: we’ll record the walkthrough and keep a Loom + a shared Google doc for async questions so folks in APAC can review.
- Security touchpoint: Naomi (cc'd) can join the security-focused session. For Bob specifically, Naomi can prep a 15-minute SOC2 / infra security overview that references the questionnaire you received.

On scheduling: I agree two sessions is the cleanest approach. If you want a single session, we should be prepared for some attendees to join only the parts relevant to them.

Suggested logistics:
- Eng session (live): Thu Mar 26, 09:00 PDT / 18:00 CET / Fri Mar 27 02:00 JST — Sean (SE), Marissa (AE), Alice + engs.
- Sec/Proc session (live): Mon Mar 30, 09:00 CET / 17:00 JST / 00:00 PDT — Naomi + Bob + Carol + Jordan (procurement). We can shorten to 45 minutes.

If those two time blocks are acceptable we’ll lock them and I’ll prepare a short architecture slide deck and a breakout plan.

—
Sean Gallagher
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
